issues.feedback: `tokio::process::Child::id()` returns `Option<u32>`, unlike `std::process::Child::id()` returning `u32`. The spec should explicitly define how to handle `None` and preserve `child_pid`/`child_pgid` guarantees used by abort/CAS logic.

The spec examples use `.await.unwrap()?` for `spawn_blocking` and `child.kill().await?` in cleanup paths. That can introduce panics/fail-fast behavior not present today. Require explicit `JoinError` mapping to `RalphError` and keep cleanup operations best-effort (warn + continue) where current code is non-fatal.

Option A is directionally correct but under-specified. It should enumerate all runtime call sites that must be wrapped, not just poll/claim. Include completion/PR/worktree paths (`has_diff`, `push_branch`, `find_existing_pr`, `create_pr`, `update_terminal_labels_best_effort`, `post_idempotent_comment`, `create/remove/reconcile_worktree`, etc.) so no blocking command is missed.

Acceptance criteria currently require `cargo test` and `clippy`, but daemon behavior is primarily guarded by conformance tests. Add an explicit gate for daemon validate tests (at least `./result/bin/ralph validate --bin ./result/bin/ralph --filter daemon`) to ensure external behavior truly remains unchanged.
